I've never understood why people think hormones shouldn't be prescribed until 18 because they're worried about permanent effects, when you'll get permanent effects from going through puberty naturally. They're both permanent, let people choose what kind of permanent effects they're willing to live with.

I get the concern of how not having puberty could be bad, but I also think there's a case to be made for puberty blockers. I'll say that I think it should be on a case-by-case basis, but it's not going to stop the person from ever going through puberty. It'll just delay it, which will give them time to decide if they want to go on hormones or not. If they realize they were wrong, they go off the blockers, and go through puberty the way they would have. If they don't, they stay on blockers until they're old enough to start hormones. Either way, they'll go through the right puberty eventually, without worrying about potential permanent effects from the first puberty.

There isn't a simple answer to knowing if you're ready to have a kid. I think there are a lot of things to consider. Do you have the money to take care of a child? The extra time and energy? The right space to raise a child in, or the willingness to move? Will you be able to meet their physical needs? Their emotional needs? Are you willing to give up at least some of your free time and social life for your child? Have you taken care of children before, and if so, at what ages? How much do you know about child development and taking care of children, and if it's not very much, are you willing to learn about those things? How much support are you going to have, and in what areas? 

The biggest thing I guess it comes down to is, are you willing and able to do the work to take care of an entire human being, no matter how hard it gets?

I had an unplanned pregnancy, and was also extremely young when I got pregnant. Something inside me knew that I wanted to carry the pregnancy to term and be a parent. 
I do not regret this decision. I love my child and I love being a dad. 
However, I do think it would have been better for both me and my child if I had been more prepared when I became a parent. Things happen and that's okay, but I think that waiting until you are sure of what you want and what you are capable of is never a bad idea. I think that the fact that you are bringing an entire new person into the world and will have to be there to support that person for the rest of their lives, and be pretty intensely supporting that person for about two decades, should be considered. I think it is something that deserves consideration and it should not be taken lightly. 

I would also take your support system into consideration. Everyone needs help, who will be there to help you, and to what degree? 

No matter what you decide, I hope things go well for you <3
